_doc: Module-specific validation rules loaded at runtime by build_gate.py. Keeps route names, variable names, and feature-specific trigger strings OUT of core Python gate logic. Add a new entry here whenever a recurring per-feature validation pattern is discovered. Do NOT put these patterns directly in build_gate.py.

_schema.body_guard: Find 'anchor' string in 'target', scan 'body_chars' chars after it. Fire when guard_pattern absent (and optionally fail_pattern present).
_schema.presence_guard: Fire when any of 'trigger_any' strings appear in 'target' AND guard_pattern is absent from full target.
_schema.tsx_autoload: Fire when route_substr appears in index.tsx AND is NOT referenced inside a useEffect (only inside click handlers).

checks.error_message: app.py ensemble includes `owm_temp` unconditionally in `temps = [owm_temp, om_temp]`. When OWM fails, owm_temp=0.0 is averaged with the valid Open-Meteo reading — temperature displayed is ~half actual value. Fix: track `owm_succeeded = True` only when OWM returns status 200, then `temps = [t for t in [owm_temp if owm_succeeded else None, om_temp] if t is not None]`. Per WEATHER API FAILED-CALL ZERO EXCLUSION MANDATE.

/weather/hourly route has no Open-Meteo fallback. When OWM fails (bad key / misconfigured URL), `items=[]` and the frontend shows 'Hourly data unavailable'. Open-Meteo provides free 48h hourly with no key. Add fallback: `if not items:` fetch `https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?...&hourly=temperature_2m,...` and parse into the items list. Per HOURLY FORECAST OPEN-METEO FALLBACK MANDATE.

SEISMIC PRECURSOR AUTO-LOAD MANDATE violated — `/precursor/analysis` is fetched ONLY inside a button click handler, never in a `useEffect` on mount. The Cross-Domain Precursor Analysis panel is empty on initial page load and only fills when the user clicks 'Generate'. Fix: call `fetchPrecursor()` inside the seismic view's mount `useEffect` alongside `fetchData()`. The button should be 'Refresh Analysis', not the only trigger. Per SEISMIC PRECURSOR AUTO-LOAD MANDATE.

PLASMA PARSING ROBUSTNESS MANDATE violated — plasma row filter uses `row[1] is not None` but does not also exclude empty string `''`. NOAA returns '' for missing speed values; `float('')` throws ValueError and the outer except resets speed to 0.0, displaying '0 km/s' or '1 km/s' which is physically impossible. Fix: `row[1] not in ('', None, '-', 'null')` AND `row[2] not in ('', None, '-', 'null')` in the filter. NEVER apply a numeric threshold (e.g. `< 50.0`) to null out parsed values — quiet-sun conditions produce legitimately low readings (300 km/s is valid solar wind). Return `None` ONLY when the API call itself fails or the response contains no usable rows.

FIRMS URL MANDATE violated — NASA FIRMS API call does not use the global `world` country code. Using a country-specific code (e.g., USA, CAN) returns only fires in that country, causing the Hazard Center to show 0 active wildfires globally despite thousands of fires burning worldwide. Fix: replace the country code segment with `world`: `https://firms.modaps.eosdis.nasa.gov/api/country/csv/{key}/VIIRS_SNPP_NRT/world/1`. Per FIRMS CSV CONTRACT in rules.md.

ASTRONOMY TIMEOUT MANDATE violated — the /astronomy/stars route does not specify a timeout >= 20s on its httpx client. The ESA Gaia TAP service regularly takes 20-30 seconds to return 2000 star records. With the default 15s httpx timeout, the request silently fails and the frontend shows 'Data acquisition timed out after 10 seconds'. Fix: use `httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=30.0)` in both /astronomy/stars and /astronomy/skyview routes. Per ASTRONOMY API TIMEOUT MANDATE.

OCEAN CURRENT VECTORS MANDATE violated — the /ocean/current route does not return per-point current vector data (`current_vectors` array or `ocean_current_direction` field). Without directional data for multiple ocean points, the frontend renders all current arrows pointing in the exact same direction (single global bearing applied uniformly), which is scientifically meaningless. Fix: fetch `ocean_current_velocity` and `ocean_current_direction` from Open-Meteo Marine API (`https://marine-api.open-meteo.com/v1/marine?hourly=ocean_current_velocity,ocean_current_direction`) and return a `current_vectors` list with per-point `{lat, lon, speed_kt, direction_deg}` entries for at least 6 major ocean basin sample points. Per OCEAN CURRENT MULTI-POINT MANDATE.

MARINE FORECAST AUTOLOAD MANDATE violated — the /ocean/current route does not fetch or return a `daily_forecast` array. The 7-Day Marine Forecast panel shows 'Awaiting 7-day extended marine forecast telemetry' indefinitely because no forecast data is included in the response. Fix: add a concurrent fetch to Open-Meteo Marine API with `daily=wave_height_max,wave_period_max,wind_speed_10m_max,visibility_mean&forecast_days=7` and return the results as `daily_forecast: [{date, wave_height_ft, wave_period_s, wind_speed_mph, visibility_mi}]` alongside the existing current conditions data. Per MARINE FORECAST AUTOLOAD MANDATE.

SPACE WEATHER COMPLETE TELEMETRY MANDATE violated — the /space/current route does not fetch solar flare data from NOAA SWPC. The Solar Activity panel shows 'Awaiting Telemetry' for Solar Flares (24h) and Radio Flux (10.7cm) because these endpoints are never called. Fix: add concurrent fetches to (1) `{NOAA_SWPC_URL}/json/goes/primary/xrays-1-day.json` for solar flare counts, (2) `{NOAA_SWPC_URL}/json/f107_cm_flux.json` for radio flux sfu value. Return `solar_flares_24h: {X: int, M: int, C: int}` and `radio_flux_sfu: float` in the response. Per SPACE WEATHER COMPLETE TELEMETRY MANDATE.

AI LAB MODEL COMPARISON AUTOLOAD MANDATE violated — the /ailab/models route does not return a `comparison_points` array with per-model temperature data. The Ensemble Forecast Divergence chart renders empty because it has no data to display. Fix: fetch Open-Meteo with multiple models concurrently using `models=gfs_seamless,ecmwf_ifs04,icon_seamless` and return `comparison_points: [{hour_label, gfs_temp, ecmwf_temp, icon_temp}]` for the next 24 hours. Use OPEN_METEO_SUITE_URL env var (default: https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast). Per AI LAB MODEL COMPARISON AUTOLOAD MANDATE.

WEATHER FORECAST CONDITION ICON MANDATE violated — index.tsx renders hourly or daily forecast cards but contains no weather condition icon mapping function. Forecast cards show only text descriptions ('Moderate rain', 'Clear sky') with no visual icons. Fix: implement `function getConditionIcon(description: string): React.ReactNode` that maps description substrings to lucide-react icons (CloudLightning for thunder, CloudRain for rain, Cloud for cloudy, Sun for clear, Eye for fog). Call this function inside every hourly card and every 14-day card JSX to render the icon above the temperature. Per WEATHER FORECAST CONDITION ICON MANDATE.

SOLAR WIND LIVE DATA MANDATE violated — the /space/current route applies a numeric minimum-value threshold (e.g. `if solar_wind_speed < 50: solar_wind_speed = None`) that nullifies valid quiet-sun solar wind readings. During quiet solar conditions, real solar wind speed is 300-500 km/s and Bz / flux values legitimately approach zero. Applying a threshold kills these valid readings and causes 'Sensor Offline' to display even when NOAA SWPC is fully operational. Fix: REMOVE the numeric threshold entirely. Return `None` ONLY when the API call fails or the response contains no usable data rows (empty string, null, '-'). The `NEVER` rule from SOLAR WIND LIVE DATA MANDATE must be enforced here. Per SOLAR WIND LIVE DATA MANDATE.

AI LAB WHAT-IF SCENARIO AUTOLOAD MANDATE violated — the What-If Scenario tab contains a chart (Model Divergence Simulation / GFS vs ECMWF Sensitivity) but the base model data is never fetched in a useEffect on mount. The chart shows empty on initial load because comparison_points data only arrives when the slider is moved. Fix: fetch `/ailab/models?lat={lat}&lon={lon}` inside a `useEffect(() => { fetchModels(); }, [lat, lon])` so the base GFS/ECMWF temperature lines render immediately on tab load. The slider adjusts an `offset` applied to this pre-loaded baseline — it does NOT trigger a new API call. Per AI LAB MODEL COMPARISON AUTOLOAD MANDATE.

PATTERN STUDIO NODE CLICK DETAIL MANDATE violated — the Pattern Studio topology renders persona nodes (Dr. Lena Vance, Gale Hawthorne, etc.) and ANOMALY/NOMINAL labels, but node onClick handlers are absent or do not update any state (selectedNode / nodeDetail / setSelected). Clicking a node does nothing. Fix: add `onClick={() => setSelectedNode(persona)}` to every node element; render a side panel or modal showing the persona's domain report text from `precursorData.domain_reports[personaName]`, their signal status badge, and the anomaly keywords. The Convergence Core node must show the full synthesis text on click. The detail panel must be dismissible. Per PATTERN STUDIO NODE CLICK DETAIL MANDATE.

RADAR FORECAST FRAMES MANDATE violated — the frontend radar timeline references past frames but does not reference `nowcast_frames` or `isForecast`. Even if the backend correctly returns `nowcast_frames`, the frontend will show 'No forecast data' if it only reads `past_frames` from the response. Fix: merge both arrays: `const allFrames = [...(data.past_frames||[]).map(f=>({...f,isForecast:false})), ...(data.nowcast_frames||[]).map(f=>({...f,isForecast:true}))]; setFrames(allFrames);`. Label forecast frames with 'Forecast' prefix on the timestamp. The timeline slider must cover all frames. Per RADAR FORECAST FRAMES MANDATE.

RADAR FRAME VARIABLE SCOPE MANDATE violated — RainViewer radar frame data is stored in a plain `let` variable or closure-scoped variable instead of a `useRef`. Variables like `allFrames`, `radarFrames`, or `frames` that are set inside a fetch callback (or useEffect) and then READ by animation timers or event handlers MUST use `useRef` to persist across renders and be accessible outside the declaring scope. A plain `let allFrames = []` declared inside a useEffect IS NOT ACCESSIBLE in onClick handlers or setInterval callbacks defined elsewhere — this causes `allFrames is not defined` ReferenceError crashes when the user clicks Play. Fix: replace `let allFrames = []` with `const allFramesRef = useRef<any[]>([])`, assign via `allFramesRef.current = frames` inside the fetch, and read via `allFramesRef.current[index]` in the animation handler. Per RADAR FRAME VARIABLE SCOPE MANDATE.

PATTERN STUDIO PERSONA ITERATION MANDATE violated — the Pattern Studio topology is NOT mapping over all domain personas to render satellite nodes. When only 1 node appears it means the code hardcodes a single node or references a single persona by name instead of iterating over the full personas array. Fix: define a `const domainPersonas = [{ name: '...', role: '...' }, ...]` array containing ALL module personas and render satellite nodes with `domainPersonas.map((persona, i) => ...)`, positioning each node radially around the SYNTHESIS CORE using `Math.cos` / `Math.sin` with evenly spaced angles (`(i / domainPersonas.length) * 2 * Math.PI`). Every persona must appear as a satellite node. Per PATTERN STUDIO PERSONA ITERATION MANDATE.

PATTERN STUDIO CANVAS OVERFLOW MANDATE violated — the Pattern Studio topology canvas does not set a minimum height tall enough to display all persona nodes without clipping. With 7 nodes arranged in a radial layout, the bottom node is cut off when the canvas is less than 450px tall. Fix: set the topology container to `style={{minHeight:'500px', overflow:'visible'}}` or `className='min-h-[500px] overflow-visible'` so all nodes are fully visible without scrolling. Per PATTERN STUDIO CANVAS OVERFLOW MANDATE.

PATTERN STUDIO NODE HOVER STABILITY MANDATE violated — topology satellite nodes use CSS scale transforms on hover (`hover:scale-*`, `transition-transform scale-*`). These cause nodes to visually jump/jitter because scaling an absolutely-positioned element shifts its visual center, triggering a mouseLeave event mid-hover and creating a seizure-like oscillation. Fix: remove all `hover:scale-*`, `transition-transform`, and `scale-*` classes from topology node containers. Use border-color or background-color changes on hover instead. Per PATTERN STUDIO NODE HOVER STABILITY MANDATE.

HAZARD FLOOD MARKERS MANDATE violated — the Hazard Center shows a flood count in the summary cards but no flood markers appear on the map. Flood data is fetched but the frontend renders zero Leaflet markers/circles for flood events. Fix: when flood data is available (from GDACS, reliefweb, or OpenWeatherMap), plot each flood event as a `L.circle([lat, lon], {color:'#3b82f6', fillOpacity:0.4, radius:50000})` on the Hazard map layer with a popup showing location name, severity, and date. If the API returns a count-only response with no coordinates, display a sidebar list of flood events instead. Per HAZARD FLOOD MARKERS MANDATE.

NULLISH COALESCING OR PRECEDENCE violated — index.tsx mixes `??` and `||` at the same expression level without parentheses (e.g. `val ?? fallback || default`). esbuild rejects this as a hard syntax error and aborts the entire bundle. Fix: wrap the nullish expression in parentheses: `(val ?? fallback) || default`. Per NULLISH COALESCING OR PRECEDENCE MANDATE.

FORECAST DAY/NIGHT EXPANSION MANDATE violated — the 14-day forecast cards expand but show only a single combined panel with no day/night split. When a day card is clicked/expanded, it MUST reveal TWO labeled sub-panels: (1) 'Daytime' with Sun icon showing high temp, day description, UV index, wind, and sunrise, and (2) 'Overnight' with Moon icon showing low temp, night description, humidity, and sunset. Fix: the backend /weather/daily route must return `day_temp`, `night_temp`, `day_description`, `night_description` per day entry. The frontend expansion JSX must render both panels side-by-side. Per FORECAST DAY/NIGHT EXPANSION MANDATE.

STAR MAP NASA IMAGERY RULE violated — the Star Map / Planetary Explorer view renders only synthetic dot-canvas stars instead of real NASA SkyView imagery. The canvas shows 'Deep sky imagery unavailable — showing chart only' permanently because no /astronomy/skyview fetch is made and ctx.drawImage() is never called. Fix: (1) add a backend /astronomy/skyview route that fetches from NASA SkyView `https://skyview.gsfc.nasa.gov/current/cgi/runquery.pl?Survey=DSS2+Red&Position={ra},{dec}&Size=2&Pixels=512&Return=PNG` and returns `{image_url: base64_data_url}`; (2) the frontend MUST fetch /astronomy/skyview and call `ctx.drawImage(img, 0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height)` to render the real telescope image behind the star dots. Per DEEP-SKY IMAGERY FALLBACK CHAIN MANDATE and RULES.MD COMPLIANCE GATE RULE.

SEISMIC DATA SHAPE CONTRACT violated — the Seismic view does not read `data.earthquakes` from the /seismic/feed response. The frontend likely reads `data.features` (raw USGS GeoJSON format) but the backend transforms the response into a flat `earthquakes` array. This mismatch means zero markers are plotted and the live feed shows 'No recent events detected' even when the backend returns hundreds of events. Fix: (1) backend /seismic/feed MUST return `{earthquakes: [{lat, lon, magnitude, depth_km, place, time_str}], count: N}`, (2) frontend MUST read `data.earthquakes` for map markers and `data.count` for the stat card. Per SEISMIC DATA SHAPE CONTRACT.

AI LAB PERSONA DEBATE DATA BINDING MANDATE violated — the Persona Debate tab uses a separate state variable from the Pattern Studio topology for precursor data. Both tabs must share a single `precursorData` state populated by `/precursor/analysis`. Separate `debateData` / `setDebateData` state that fetches the same endpoint creates desync where one tab loads and the other shows 'Awaiting domain data...' indefinitely. Fix: use one `const [precursorData, setPrecursorData] = useState(null)` shared across Debate and Pattern Studio tabs. Both tabs read `precursorData?.domain_reports?.[persona.name]`. Per AI LAB PERSONA DEBATE DATA BINDING MANDATE.

PERSONA NODE STATUS CONSISTENCY MANDATE violated — persona nodes can show 'ANOMALY' status visually but clicking them shows 'baseline nominal' because the node label status and the domain_report text are sourced from different data fields. Fix: node status badge (ANOMALY/NOMINAL) must be derived from the SAME field as the modal report text — use `precursorData.domain_reports[persona.name]` for both. If the status is ANOMALY, the report text must contain keywords like 'anomaly', 'elevated', 'unusual', or 'detected'. If no domain_reports key exists for a persona, default status to NOMINAL. Per PERSONA NODE STATUS CONSISTENCY MANDATE.

AI LAB MODEL COMPARE CHART BINDING violated — the Model Compare tab fetches /ailab/models (which returns 200 with comparison_points) but renders 'No model data available' because the frontend does not read `data.comparison_points` to populate the chart. Fix: (1) after fetching /ailab/models, set state with `data.comparison_points` — NOT `data.models` or `data.data`; (2) feed `comparison_points` array directly to the Recharts LineChart as `<LineChart data={comparisonPoints}>` where each point has `{hour, gfs_temp, ecmwf_temp, icon_temp, hrrr_temp}`; (3) ensure the useEffect fetches on component mount with the current lat/lon. FORBIDDEN: reading any field other than `comparison_points` from the /ailab/models response for chart data.

OCEANIC WAVE DATA BINDING violated — the Oceanic Intelligence page shows '--' for Wave Height and Swell Direction because the frontend does not read `wave_height` / `swell_direction` from the /ocean/current response. Fix: (1) backend /ocean/current MUST return `{wave_height: float, wave_period: float, swell_direction: float, swell_direction_label: str, swell_height: float, sea_surface_temp: float, current_speed: float, current_direction: float}` — fetch wave data from Open-Meteo Marine API (`https://marine-api.open-meteo.com/v1/marine?latitude={lat}&longitude={lon}&current=wave_height,wave_period,swell_wave_height,swell_wave_direction`); (2) frontend MUST render `oceanData.wave_height` and `oceanData.swell_direction_label` in the header stat cards — NEVER '--' when the route returns 200. Per OCEANIC WAVE DATA MANDATE.

RADAR FORECAST FRAMES MANDATE violated — the radar timeline shows only past frames (Past: 13, Future: 0) because `radar.nowcast` frames are ignored. The RainViewer API returns both `radar.past` and `radar.nowcast` arrays. Fix: merge both arrays: `const allFrames = [...(data.radar.past||[]).map(f=>({...f,isForecast:false})), ...(data.radar.nowcast||[]).map(f=>({...f,isForecast:true}))]`; label the counter as `Past: N frames | Forecast: M frames` using `isForecast` flag; render forecast frame timestamps with 'Forecast' prefix instead of 'No forecast data'. FORBIDDEN: using only `radar.past` and ignoring `radar.nowcast`. Per RADAR FORECAST FRAMES MANDATE.

SEISMIC TIMESTAMP TIMEZONE MANDATE violated — the /seismic/feed route formats earthquake times using `datetime.fromtimestamp()` which silently converts UTC millisecond timestamps to the server's local timezone (EDT, PST, etc.) with no timezone label. This makes a 06:58 PM UTC earthquake display as 06:58 PM local — a 12+ hour ambiguity; users cannot tell if the event is recent or 12 hours old. Fix: (1) replace `datetime.fromtimestamp(time_ms / 1000.0)` with `datetime.utcfromtimestamp(time_ms / 1000.0)`; (2) format as `'%m/%d %I:%M %p UTC'` so the date AND timezone are always visible (e.g., '04/28 10:58 PM UTC'); (3) NEVER display seismic event times without a UTC suffix. Per SEISMIC TIMESTAMP TIMEZONE MANDATE.

HAZARD FLOOD DATA MANDATE violated — the /hazards/ route does not fetch or return any flood event data. The Hazard Center is missing the Floods category entirely: no flood count card, no flood markers on the map, no Floods layer toggle. Fix: (1) fetch active flood events from ReliefWeb API (`https://api.reliefweb.int/v1/disasters?filter[field]=type.name&filter[value]=Flood&limit=20&fields[]=name,country,date,status,primary_country`) OR parse GDACS RSS (`https://www.gdacs.org/xml/rss.xml`) filtering for type FL; (2) return `floods: [{lat, lon, name, severity, date}]` and `flood_count: int` in the response payload alongside earthquakes/storms/wildfires; (3) frontend MUST render flood markers as `L.circle([lat,lon], {color:'#3b82f6', fillOpacity:0.4, radius:60000})` on a dedicated togglable Floods layer; (4) add a Floods count card in the summary header. FORBIDDEN: a Hazard Center without flood tracking. Per HAZARD FLOOD DATA MANDATE.

AI LAB MODEL COMPARISON RESILIENCE MANDATE violated — the /ailab/models route calls `raise_for_status()` on the Open-Meteo multi-model request. HRRR only covers CONUS (lat 20-55, lon -130 to -60); for any coordinate outside North America Open-Meteo returns HTTP 400, `raise_for_status()` throws, the except catches it, and the chart renders 'No model data available'. Fix: (1) remove `raise_for_status()` and check `res.status_code == 200`; (2) if any per-model temp list is empty, exclude it from comparison_points — do NOT set the value to None or 0; (3) fall back to global-only models (gfs_seamless, ecmwf_ifs04, icon_seamless) without hrrr when the coordinate is outside HRRR coverage (`lat < 20 or lat > 55 or lon < -130 or lon > -60`); (4) the chart MUST render with at least 2 model lines whenever Open-Meteo returns 200. Per AI LAB MODEL COMPARISON RESILIENCE MANDATE.

LEAFLET INVALIDATE SIZE MANDATE violated — Leaflet map is initialized via callback ref or useEffect but `invalidateSize()` is never called. In flex/grid layouts the map container reaches its final pixel dimensions AFTER Leaflet's internal layout pass, causing the map to render split in half — tiles appear in the top portion only and the bottom shows a blank or duplicated strip. Fix: immediately after `mapInstanceRef.current = L.map(node, {...})` in the callback ref, add `setTimeout(() => mapInstanceRef.current?.invalidateSize(), 150)`. This forces Leaflet to recalculate its container dimensions after the browser layout engine settles. EVERY Leaflet map initialization block MUST include this setTimeout invalidateSize call. Per LEAFLET INVALIDATE SIZE MANDATE.

WEATHER WIND HUMIDITY MANDATE violated — the /weather/current route does not extract `wind_speed`, `wind_deg`, or `humidity` from the OWM One Call 3.0 response. The Wind and Humidity cards display '--' because these fields are absent from the returned JSON. OWM One Call 3.0 returns these under `current.wind_speed` (m/s), `current.wind_deg` (degrees), `current.humidity` (%), and `current.wind_gust` (m/s). Fix: extract all four fields, convert wind_speed and wind_gust from m/s to mph (multiply by 2.23694), and return `wind_speed_mph`, `wind_gust_mph`, `wind_deg`, `humidity`, `dew_point` in the response. Per WEATHER WIND HUMIDITY MANDATE.

WEATHER CITY GEOCODING BACKEND MANDATE violated — the /weather/current route does not call OWM reverse geocoding to resolve coordinates to a city name. The hero displays raw coordinates (e.g. '41.44, -73.21') instead of 'Poughkeepsie, NY'. Fix: after fetching current conditions, make a concurrent call to `https://api.openweathermap.org/geo/1.0/reverse?lat={lat}&lon={lon}&limit=1&appid={OPEN_WEATHER_MAP_KEY}` and extract `name` (city) and `state` from the first result. Return `city_name: f'{name}, {state}'` (or just `name` for non-US locations) in the response JSON. The frontend hero MUST display this field. Per WEATHER CITY GEOCODING RULE.

HOURLY FORECAST TIMEZONE MANDATE violated — the /weather/hourly route formats OWM timestamps with `utcfromtimestamp()` or `strftime` without applying the `timezone_offset` field returned by OWM One Call 3.0. OWM returns UTC Unix timestamps; the response root contains `timezone_offset` (integer seconds). A user at UTC-4 (EDT) seeing 11am local time will see hourly cards starting at '03:00 PM' because the display shows UTC time. Fix: read `timezone_offset = data.get('timezone_offset', 0)` from the OWM response, add it to each hourly `dt` before formatting: `local_dt = datetime.utcfromtimestamp(h['dt'] + timezone_offset)`, then format with `local_dt.strftime('%I:%M %p')`. Per HOURLY FORECAST TIMEZONE MANDATE.

FLOOD COORDINATE EXTRACTION MANDATE violated — the /hazards/summary route counts flood events but does NOT extract `lat`/`lon` per flood. The response returns only `active_floods_count: int` with no coordinate array, so the Hazard Center map renders zero flood markers despite showing '7 Flood Warnings' in the summary card. Fix: parse each GDACS flood entry for `<georss:point>` or `<gdacs:latitude>`/`<gdacs:longitude>` tags and return `floods: [{lat, lon, title, severity, date}]` in the response alongside the count. Every parsed flood entry that has coordinates MUST appear in this array. Per HAZARD FLOOD MARKERS MANDATE.

OCEAN WAVE IMPERIAL CONVERSION MANDATE violated — the /ocean/current route returns wave height from Open-Meteo Marine API without converting from meters to feet. Open-Meteo Marine always returns wave_height in meters regardless of any unit parameter. The frontend displays '0.0 ft' or a decimal fraction because 0.5m is rendered as '0.5 ft' — a 67% underreport. Fix: multiply every wave_height value by 3.28084 before returning: `wave_height_ft = round(wave_data.get('wave_height', 0) * 3.28084, 1)`. Apply the same conversion to daily_forecast wave heights. NEVER rely on a `length_unit=imperial` query param — it is not supported by the Marine API. Per OCEAN WAVE IMPERIAL CONVERSION MANDATE.

SEISMIC MAP HEIGHT MANDATE violated — the SeismicView Leaflet map container does not have an explicit pixel height. Leaflet requires a fixed pixel height on its container div; without it the container collapses to 0px in a flex layout and the map renders blank (dark rectangle with no tiles). Fix: add `style={{height:'500px'}}` or `className='h-[500px]'` to the seismic map container div. The map MUST also call `invalidateSize()` in a 150ms setTimeout after `L.map(node, {...})`. Per SEISMIC MAP HEIGHT MANDATE.

AI LAB WHAT-IF BACKEND ROUTE MANDATE violated — the What-If Scenario tab has sliders for temperature anomaly forcing, moisture advection, and deep layer shear, but no backend route exists to compute projected model divergence. The 'Projected Divergence' panel shows 'No scenario data available' permanently. Fix: add `@router.post('/ailab/whatif')` accepting `{lat: float, lon: float, temp_offset: float, moisture_offset: float, shear_offset: float}` and returning `{gfs_points: [{hour, temp}], ecmwf_points: [{hour, temp}]}` where each series is the base model forecast (from /ailab/models) shifted by the provided offsets. The frontend must POST to this endpoint whenever a slider value changes (debounced 300ms). Per AI LAB WHAT-IF SCENARIO MANDATE.

MARINE FORECAST WIND VISIBILITY MANDATE violated — the /ocean/current route fetches daily marine forecast but does NOT include `wind_speed_10m_max` or `visibility_mean` in the Open-Meteo Marine daily request. The 7-Day Marine Forecast cards show '--' for Wind and Vis because these fields are missing from the API call. Fix: add `wind_speed_10m_max,visibility_mean` to the `daily=` parameter of the Open-Meteo Marine API request and return them as `wind_speed_mph` (multiply by 2.23694 for m/s→mph) and `visibility_mi` (multiply by 0.000621371 for meters→miles) in each daily_forecast entry. Per MARINE FORECAST WIND VISIBILITY MANDATE.

FORECAST DESCRIPTION TRUNCATION MANDATE violated — the 14-day forecast component uses CSS `truncate` or `text-ellipsis` on description text. This cuts the description to '...' after a few words making it unreadable (e.g. 'Anticipate moderate rain co...'). Fix: remove `truncate`, `overflow-hidden`, and `text-ellipsis` classes from description text elements in forecast day rows. Description text MUST be allowed to wrap to multiple lines. Add `whitespace-normal` and `text-sm` to ensure readable wrapping. Per FORECAST DESCRIPTION TRUNCATION MANDATE.

FORECAST DESCRIPTION LENGTH MANDATE violated — the /weather/daily route generates daily descriptions shorter than 10 words for days beyond day 7 (Open-Meteo fallback days). Descriptions like 'Forecast models suggest mixed conditions' are 5 words — below the 10-word minimum. Fix: for Open-Meteo fallback days, build the description by combining available fields: f'Expect {condition} with a {precip_pct}% chance of precipitation, high of {high}°F and low of {low}°F, winds at {wind_speed} mph.' This guarantees at least 15 words using real data. Never return a description shorter than 10 words. Per FORECAST DESCRIPTION LENGTH MANDATE.

SST NUMERIC TOOLTIP MANDATE violated — the Oceanic Intelligence map shows an SST color gradient but clicking or hovering on the map does NOT show a numeric temperature value. Users cannot read actual ocean temperatures from a color scale alone. Fix: add a Leaflet click or mousemove handler on the SST layer that shows a popup with the nearest ocean temperature data point: `L.popup().setLatLng(e.latlng).setContent('SST: ${nearestTemp}°F
${lat.toFixed(1)}°N, ${lon.toFixed(1)}°W').openOn(map)`. Additionally add a numeric legend with at least 5 temperature reference values (32°F, 50°F, 68°F, 77°F, 90°F) positioned at the bottom right. Per SST NUMERIC TOOLTIP MANDATE.

SEISMIC USGS LIVE DATA MANDATE violated — the /seismic/feed route does not include required USGS query parameters to fetch real-time earthquake data. Missing `minmagnitude=2.5`, `starttime` (7 days back), `orderby=time`, and/or `format=geojson`. Without these parameters the USGS API may return 0 results or default to a tiny result set. Fix: build the URL as `https://earthquake.usgs.gov/fdsnws/event/1/query?format=geojson&starttime={start_7d}&minmagnitude=2.5&orderby=time&limit=500` where `start_7d = (datetime.utcnow() - timedelta(days=7)).strftime('%Y-%m-%d')`. The route MUST return at minimum the count of events in the last 7 days. Per SEISMIC USGS LIVE DATA MANDATE.

SPACE WEATHER SOLAR WIND EXTRACT MANDATE violated — the /space/current route does not extract `solar_wind_speed` (km/s) from the NOAA SWPC solar wind dataset. The Solar Wind card shows '--' because the speed field is not parsed from the response. NOAA SWPC returns solar wind from `https://services.swpc.noaa.gov/products/solar-wind/plasma-7-day.json` where each row is [time_tag, density, speed, temperature]. Speed is at index 2. Fix: fetch the plasma JSON, find the most recent row where row[2] is not empty/null, and return `solar_wind_speed: float(row[2])` and `plasma_density: float(row[1])`. Also fetch mag-7-day.json for IMF Bz at index 3. Per SPACE WEATHER SOLAR WIND EXTRACT MANDATE.

AI LAB SUBTITLE GEOCODING MANDATE violated — the AI Lab subtitle displays raw coordinates ('Region: 41.43874215743339, -73.21270998284758') instead of the resolved city name. Any subtitle, header, or description that references the user's location MUST use the `city_name` field from the /weather/current response (e.g. 'Southbury, Connecticut') — NEVER raw lat/lon strings. Fix: in the AI Lab view, read `city_name` from the weather data state and render it as the location descriptor: `Analyzing data for {cityName || 'your location'}`. If city_name is unavailable, display 'your region' — never display raw coordinate numbers to the user. Per AI LAB SUBTITLE GEOCODING MANDATE.

OCEAN CURRENT VECTOR DIRECTION MANDATE violated — the Oceanic Intelligence page renders current vector arrows but does NOT apply `direction_deg` from the backend `current_vectors` array to orient each arrow. All arrows render pointing in the same default direction, making the current map scientifically meaningless and visually contradictory (arrows pointing against each other in adjacent cells). Fix: for each entry in `current_vectors`, rotate the arrow element using the `direction_deg` value — in SVG/DivIcon: `style='transform: rotate(${vec.direction_deg}deg)'`; in Canvas: `ctx.rotate(vec.direction_deg * Math.PI / 180)`. NEVER render ocean current arrows without applying per-point directional rotation from real data. Per OCEAN CURRENT VECTOR DIRECTION MANDATE.

TOFIXED NUMERIC GUARD MANDATE violated — index.tsx calls `.toFixed()` on a `?? 'N/A'` null-coalescing expression: e.g. `(p.distance_au ?? 'N/A').toFixed(3)`. When the backend returns `null`, `undefined`, or a string like 'N/A' for that field, `?? 'N/A'` kicks in and the value becomes the string 'N/A'. Calling `.toFixed()` on a string throws 'toFixed is not a function' and crashes the entire view inside ErrorBoundary. Fix: replace with `(typeof p.distance_au === 'number' ? p.distance_au.toFixed(3) : 'N/A')` — NEVER call `.toFixed()` on any expression that has a `?? 'string'` fallback. Per TOFIXED NUMERIC GUARD MANDATE.

VOLCANO ALERT LEVEL CASE MANDATE violated — app.py references `alert_level` but does NOT apply `.lower()` before comparing to `'warning'`, `'watch'`, or `'advisory'`. The USGS Volcano Hazards API returns capitalized alert level strings: `Warning`, `Watch`, `Advisory`, `Normal`. Comparing these against lowercase string literals (`in ('warning', 'watch', 'advisory')`) will always evaluate False — `'Warning' in ('warning', ...)` is False. Result: ALL volcanoes count as inactive regardless of real alert status, showing 0 Active Volcanoes even during active eruptions. Fix: normalize on extraction — `alert_level = v.get('alert_level', 'Normal').lower()` — OR compare case-insensitively: `v['alert_level'].lower() in ('warning', 'watch', 'advisory')`. Per VOLCANO ALERT LEVEL CASE MANDATE.

AI LAB PRECURSOR ROUTE MANDATE violated — index.tsx fetches a `/precursor` or `/precursor/analysis` endpoint but app.py has NO corresponding `@router.get('/precursor/analysis')` route. Result: 404 on load, Persona Debate shows 'Precursor analysis unavailable', Pattern Studio shows 'Loading topology...' forever. Root cause: AI Lab domain often generates insufficient routes (<3000 chars) when competing with 6 other domains in parallel generation. Fix: the AI Lab backend domain MUST generate `/precursor/analysis` as its primary route — this endpoint calls each persona's `.md` file to produce domain_reports, synthesizes a convergence score, and returns `{domain_reports: {PersonaName: str}, convergence_score: float, anomalies: [str], synthesis: str}`. Per AI LAB PRECURSOR ROUTE MANDATE.

WEATHER GEOLOCATION ZERO COORD MANDATE violated — the weather component uses `navigator.geolocation` BUT also calls the weather fetch immediately with initial state values (lat=0, lon=0) before geolocation resolves. This fetches weather for coordinates 0°N, 0°E (the Gulf of Guinea, off the coast of Ghana) and displays '0°F' and 'Unknown' city name. Fix: NEVER trigger weather fetch before geolocation resolves. Use `const [coords, setCoords] = useState<{lat:number,lon:number}|null>(null)` — call `setCoords({lat, lon})` in the geolocation success callback, and gate all weather fetches: `useEffect(() => { if (coords) fetchWeatherData(coords.lat, coords.lon); }, [coords])`. The fallback for geolocation failure should be a known default city (e.g. New York: lat=40.7128, lon=-74.0060) — NEVER lat=0, lon=0. Per WEATHER GEOLOCATION ZERO COORD MANDATE.

SPACE WEATHER SOLAR WIND EXTRACT MANDATE violated — the /space/current route fetches `plasma-7-day.json` but does NOT extract solar wind speed using index [2]. NOAA SWPC plasma JSON is a 2D array: the first row is always a header `['time_tag', 'density', 'speed', 'temperature']`, subsequent rows are data arrays `['2024-05-04 12:00:00', '4.2', '448.0', '56000']`. Speed is ALWAYS at index [2] of each data row — NOT a dict key. Code that does `row.get('speed')` returns None because rows are lists not dicts. Fix: skip the header row then access the last valid row: `data_rows = [r for r in plasma_json[1:] if r and len(r) > 2 and r[2] not in ('', None)]`, then `solar_wind_speed = float(data_rows[-1][2])`. Apply the same index pattern for plasma density ([1]) and mag Bz ([3] from mag-7-day.json). Per SPACE WEATHER SOLAR WIND EXTRACT MANDATE.

WEATHER CURRENT HIGH/LOW MANDATE violated — the /weather/current route does not include today's high and low temperatures in its response. The frontend hero always displays 'H: X° L: Y°' — without these fields they render as NaN. Fix: fetch today's high/low from OWM daily[0]: `high = round(owm_data.get('daily', [{}])[0].get('temp', {}).get('max', 0))` and `low = round(owm_data.get('daily', [{}])[0].get('temp', {}).get('min', 0))`. Return them as `'high': high, 'low': low` in the response payload. Per WEATHER CURRENT HIGH/LOW MANDATE.

USGS VOLCANOES LIST PARSE MANDATE violated — the volcano route fetches the USGS Volcanoes API but parses it incorrectly. The USGS endpoint `volcanoApi/volcanoes` returns a plain JSON array of volcano objects, NOT an object with a 'volcanoes' key. Code that does `volc_data.get('volcanoes', [])` will always get an empty list, showing 0 active volcanoes. Fix: parse as a list directly: `volcanoes_list = volc_data if isinstance(volc_data, list) else volc_data.get('volcanoes', [])`. Check each item's alert level field — try both `v.get('alert_level')` and `v.get('current_status', {}).get('hazard_level')` since the field name varies. Per USGS VOLCANOES LIST PARSE MANDATE.

SKYVIEW URL ENCODING MANDATE violated — `skyview.gsfc.nasa.gov` URL built without `urllib.parse.quote()` on the survey parameter. Survey names like 'DSS2 Red' contain spaces that make the URL malformed — NASA returns HTML instead of PNG. Fix: `encoded_survey = urllib.parse.quote(str(survey), safe='')` then use `?Survey={encoded_survey}&...` in the URL, OR wrap the 'Survey' key in the params dict: `'Survey': urllib.parse.quote(str(survey_param), safe='')`. Then return {'image_url': ''} if content-type is not image/*.

SKYVIEW URL ENCODING MANDATE violated — /astronomy/skyview route does not verify `resp.headers['content-type']` starts with 'image/' before base64-encoding. When NASA returns HTML (e.g. on a malformed URL), the backend base64-encodes the HTML page and the frontend silently fails with `img.onerror`. Add: `if not resp.headers.get('content-type','').startswith('image/'): return {'image_url': ''}`

OCEAN SST TILE VISIBILITY MANDATE violated — a `dark_nolabels` or `light_nolabels` CartoDB tile layer is configured with opacity > 0.3 on top of an SST/temperature data layer. Empty `onClick={() => { /* ... */ }}` found in index.tsx. At least one interactive button has a non-functional click handler (no state change). This is typically the SST layer toggle button. Every onClick MUST call a state setter or dispatch. FORBIDDEN: onClick with only a comment or empty body. Per OCEAN SST TILE VISIBILITY MANDATE.

app.py radar route fetches from RainViewer but does not parse the `radar.nowcast` array from the response. The timeline will show 'No forecast data' even though RainViewer always returns nowcast frames in `radar.nowcast`. Per RADAR FORECAST FRAMES MANDATE.

VOLCANO FEED ALERT MANDATE violated — app.py has a volcano route but does not parse `alert_level` or `color_code` from the USGS VolcanoApi response to determine active status. The USGS Volcano API (`https://volcanoes.usgs.gov/vsc/api/volcanoApi/volcanoes`) returns each volcano with `alert_level` (values: 'normal','advisory','watch','warning') and `color_code` (GREEN/YELLOW/ORANGE/RED). A volcano is 'active' when alert_level is 'advisory','watch','warning' OR color_code is 'YELLOW','ORANGE','RED'. Fix: iterate the response array and count volcanoes where `v.get('alert_level','normal').lower() in ('advisory','watch','warning')`. Return `{'volcanoes': [...], 'active_count': N}`. Per VOLCANO FEED ALERT MANDATE.

SEISMIC PRECURSOR AUTOLOAD MANDATE violated — the Seismic & Volcanic page has a cross-domain precursor analysis section but it does NOT auto-load on mount. Show a loading spinner during the fetch. Per SEISMIC PRECURSOR AUTOLOAD MANDATE.

HAZARD MAP EARTHQUAKE COLOR MANDATE violated — the Hazard Center map uses depth-based color coding for earthquake dots (orange=shallow, red=intermediate, purple=deep). This produces hundreds of orange/red/purple dots that visually collide with the category legend colors (Volcanoes=purple, Floods=blue, Wildfires=dark red). Users cannot distinguish earthquakes from other event types. Fix: remove depth-based color variation. Use a SINGLE distinct color for ALL earthquake markers (e.g. '#f59e0b' amber/gold). Depth information should only appear in the popup tooltip. Volcano markers: '#ef4444' red. Storm markers: '#06b6d4' cyan. Flood markers: '#3b82f6' blue. Wildfire markers: '#dc2626' dark red. Per HAZARD MAP EARTHQUAKE COLOR MANDATE.

Hazard Center map container uses `flex-grow`, `h-full`, or `height: 100%` / `calc(100vh - ...)` which causes the map to fill all remaining viewport space and pushes the Active Tropical Storms, Wildfire, and Flood panels below the fold with no scroll indicator. WEATHER HERO CITY DISPLAY MANDATE violated — the WeatherView component does not reference a city name field (city, cityName, city_name, locationName) in the hero section. Fallback to `${lat.toFixed(2)}°, ${lon.toFixed(2)}°` only when city is absent or 'Unknown'. Per WEATHER HERO CITY DISPLAY MANDATE.

AI LAB MODEL COMPARISON CITY MANDATE violated — the AI Lab Model Comparison subtitle shows raw coordinates ('your region | Avg spread: 0°F') because it does not use a resolved city name. OCEAN CURRENT VECTORS MANDATE violated — the ocean/current route does not return `current_vectors` data from Open-Meteo marine API. The SST map shows colors but no animated current arrows because the backend returns no vector data. Per OCEAN CURRENT VECTORS MANDATE.

SPACE WEATHER SUNSPOT MANDATE violated — the space weather route does not fetch sunspot number data. The dashboard shows 'N/A' for Sunspot Number. Fix: fetch daily sunspot number from NOAA SWPC: `https://services.swpc.noaa.gov/json/sunspot_number_daily.json` — this returns an array of `{time_tag, ssn, smoothed_ssn}` objects. Use the most recent `ssn` value. Return it as `sunspot_number` in the space weather response. Per SPACE WEATHER SUNSPOT MANDATE.

SPACE WEATHER KP FORECAST MANDATE violated — the space weather route does not fetch predicted Kp index data for the Impact Timeline. The timeline shows 'Predicted Kp data not available'. Fix: fetch 3-day Kp forecast from NOAA SWPC: `https://services.swpc.noaa.gov/products/noaa-geomagnetic-forecast.json` — this returns `[[time_tag, kp, observed, noaa_scale], ...]` rows. Parse each row's kp value (index 1) and time_tag (index 0) to build `kp_forecast: [{time: str, kp: float}]`. Return this array alongside the current kp in the response. Per SPACE WEATHER KP FORECAST MANDATE.

LLM CALL ISOLATION MANDATE violated — app.py invokes `call_llm_async(...)` inside the same `try/except` block that wraps real-API fetches (USGS, NOAA, Open-Meteo, NASA). When the LLM service hiccups (timeout, 503, JSON decode error), the surrounding bare `except Exception:` swallows the LLM failure and the route falls through to its empty-data fallback — returning HTTP 200 OK with `earthquakes: []`, `kp_index: 0.0`, `sea_surface_temp: 0.0`, etc. The frontend then displays zeros across Seismic, Space Weather, Hazards, Ocean, AI Lab Debate, Precursor Analysis even though every upstream API responded correctly. Fix: define an `async def _safe_call_llm(*args, **kwargs)` helper at module scope that wraps `await call_llm_async(*args, **kwargs)` in its OWN try/except returning `{'text': ''}` on any exception. Replace every `await call_llm_async(` call site with `await _safe_call_llm(`. This guarantees real-API data still flows to the frontend even when the LLM is offline. Per LLM CALL ISOLATION MANDATE.

PLANETARY EXPLORER STAR MAP MANDATE violated — the Planetary Explorer view does not implement a star map canvas renderer. The page shows a blank dark area. Use the Hipparcos catalogue via the Astronomy API or generate procedural stars: for i in range(200), plot random x/y at canvas dimensions with radius proportional to brightness. For planet positions from the backend, draw labeled circles at their ecliptic coordinates converted to canvas x/y. Show constellation lines for the 12 zodiac constellations. Use requestAnimationFrame for the time slider. Per PLANETARY EXPLORER STAR MAP MANDATE.
